text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word.
notes: The Greek term 'logos' is translated as 'Word.' This term carries significant theological weight and can also be understood as 'reason' or 'expression.' The translation prioritizes the traditional rendering of 'Word' to maintain consistency with established biblical translations. The phrase 'prov ton yeon' is rendered as 'with God.' The original Greek could also be interpreted as 'face to face with God,' but this translation avoids adding interpretive nuance. The repetition of 'o logov' (the Word) is maintained to reflect the original text's emphasis.

text: This one was in the beginning with God.
notes: The Greek word 'outos' can mean 'this one' or 'he'. Given the theological significance of the verse, 'this one' is the more conservative rendering. The phrase 'arch prov ton yeon' is translated as 'in the beginning with God' to maintain accuracy and avoid unnecessary elaboration. The term 'yeon' is translated as 'God' following the terminology policy.

text: All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that has been made.
notes: The phrase 'cwriv autou' is often translated as 'with him' or 'through him.' The choice of 'without him' reflects a conservative rendering emphasizing the LORD's role in creation. The phrase 'oude en o gegonen' is translated as 'nothing was made that has been made' to maintain accuracy and clarity for the target audience.

text: In him was life, and the life was the light of humanity.
notes: The Greek word 'zwh' is translated as 'life.' It carries a sense of vitality and existence. 'fwv' is translated as 'light,' representing illumination and revelation. 'anyrwpwn' is translated as 'humanity,' encompassing all people. The phrase 'the light of humanity' is a conservative rendering of the Greek, avoiding interpretations that might limit the light's scope to individual people.

text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.
notes: The verb 'katelaben' can mean 'comprehend,' 'grasp,' or 'receive.' In this context, 'comprehend' is the most conservative and theologically sound rendering, reflecting the inability of the darkness to understand the light's nature and purpose. The imperfect tense indicates a continuous or repeated action; the darkness consistently fails to grasp the light.

text: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.
notes: The phrase 'apestalmenov para yeou' is commonly translated as 'sent by God.' A more literal rendering would be 'sent from God,' which is used here to maintain precision. The pronoun 'autw' refers to the man, John, and is translated as 'whose name was.'

text: He declared and testified that he might testify concerning the light, so that all might believe through him.
notes: The verb 'marturhsh' appears twice, both translated as 'testify' to maintain the emphasis on witness. The phrase 'di autou' is translated as 'through him' to reflect the instrumental agency of Jesus in enabling belief. There is no ambiguity in this verse.

text: He was not the light, but to testify concerning the light.
notes: The verb 'marturhsh' is translated as 'testify' to maintain precision. It conveys the idea of bearing witness to something, rather than simply 'witnessing' it. The phrase 'peri tou fwtov' is rendered as 'concerning the light' to avoid any implication of being 'about' the light in a more general sense.

text: He was the true light, which gives light to every man coming into the world.
notes: The term 'true light' (alhyinon) can also be translated as 'genuine light' or 'real light.' The choice of 'true' emphasizes authenticity and distinction. The verb 'fwtiizei' is translated as 'gives light' to convey the active role of the light in illuminating. The phrase 'coming into the world' is a literal rendering of 'ercomenon eiv ton kosmon.'

text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word became the world, and the world did not know it.
notes: The phrase 'egeneto' is translated as 'became' to reflect the sense of origin and manifestation. The verb 'egnō' is translated as 'know' to maintain the original meaning of recognition or understanding. The order of clauses is adjusted for clarity and readability in English.

text: He came to his own, but his own did not receive him.
notes: The phrase 'his own' (idia) appears twice. It refers to the Jewish people, to whom the Logos (Word) was coming. The verb 'parelabon' can mean 'receive' or 'accept.' The translation uses 'receive' as the more conservative and direct rendering. There is theological significance in the rejection of the Logos by his own people.

text: Those who received him gave authority to the believers to become children of God, those who believe in his name.
notes: The verb 'edwken' (gave) can also mean 'granted.' The choice of 'gave authority' is conservative and avoids implying a transfer of inherent power.

The phrase 'tekna yeou genesyai' is translated as 'become children of God.' This rendering emphasizes the transformative nature of faith, aligning with established theological interpretations. An alternative, 'are born children of God,' was considered but rejected for its potential to imply a biological origin.
The phrase 'toiv pisteuousin eiv to onoma autou' is translated as 'those who believe in his name.' This is a standard rendering that avoids unnecessary complexity.

text: They were not born of natural descent, nor of human will, nor of a man’s decision, but of God.
notes: The phrase 'of natural descent' (ek yelhmatwn sarkov) is a standard rendering of the Greek, reflecting a contrast with spiritual birth. 'Human will' (ek yelhmatov androv) is translated literally. 'Decision' (yelhmatov) is used to convey the sense of a deliberate act or plan. The verse emphasizes that Jesus' birth was not a product of human agency but a divine act.

text: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
notes: The phrase 'dwelt among us' is a rendering of 'eskhnwsen en hmin,' which can also be translated as 'tabernacled among us.' Given the theological significance of this verse, a more straightforward rendering was chosen to avoid potential misinterpretations related to the concept of tabernacles. 'Eyeasameya' is translated as 'beheld' to convey the sense of direct observation and recognition of the glory. 'Monogenouv' is translated as 'only Son' to maintain accuracy and avoid potentially confusing terms like 'unique.' 'Plhrhv caritov kai alhyeiav' is rendered as 'full of grace and truth' to reflect the standard understanding of this phrase.

text: I testify about him, declaring that this was the one who said, ‘He who comes after me is greater than I,’ for he was before me.
notes: The verb 'kekragen' is difficult to render precisely. It implies a declaration or testimony, but also carries a sense of having been proclaimed or asserted. 'Declaring' was chosen to convey both aspects. The phrase 'was before me' is a conservative rendering of 'emprosyen mou gegonen,' emphasizing the temporal priority of the one being testified about. The original Greek uses a perfect tense, suggesting a state of being already established.
The use of 'greater than I' is a direct translation of 'opisw mou ercomenov emprosyen mou,' maintaining the original's emphasis on relative position and importance.

text: And from his fullness we all received grace upon grace.
notes: The phrase 'carin anti caritov' is unusual. It literally means 'grace instead of grace.' A conservative rendering understands this as 'grace upon grace,' indicating an abundance or intensification of grace. Other interpretations are possible, but this choice avoids adding theological nuance not explicitly present in the Greek.

text: Through Moses the law was given; through Jesus Christ grace and truth came.
notes: The Greek word 'cariv' is typically translated as 'grace.' The choice to use 'grace' here reflects its common theological understanding. The Greek word 'alhyeia' is typically translated as 'truth.' The phrase 'grace and truth came' is a standard rendering of this sequence, emphasizing the dual nature of Christ's revelation. The verb 'egeneto' is translated as 'came,' which is a conservative rendering conveying the idea of manifestation or becoming.

text: He declared, the only begotten Son, who was with the Father, made it known.
notes: The verb 'exhghsato' is translated as 'made it known' to convey the sense of revelation without implying a specific method of communication. The term 'monogenhv' is translated as 'only begotten' to reflect the traditional understanding of the term, acknowledging the theological significance and potential for varied interpretations. The phrase 'with the Father' is rendered literally to maintain accuracy.

text: This was the testimony of John when the Jews from Jerusalem, priests and Levites, sent to ask him, 'Who are you?'
He confessed and denied, and confessed that he was not the Christ.
They asked him, “Are you the one who is to come?” He said, “I am not.”
Then He asked them, “Who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us, concerning what they say about you?”
I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, making ready the way of the LORD, as Isaiah the prophet said.
And those who were sent were from the Pharisees.
They asked him and said to him, “Why do you baptize if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”
John answered, saying, “I baptize you in water, but among you stands one whom you do not know.
He who is coming after me is greater than I. I am not worthy to loosen the sandals of his feet.
This happened in Bethany beyond the Jordan where John was baptizing.
The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, 'Behold, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.'
This is about what I said: someone is coming after me, who was before me. He was already in front of me.
And he was not for the purpose that he should be the Christ, but that he might make Israel known through him. Therefore, I was baptized in the water.
John testified, saying, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it remained on him.”

And he did not say to him, ‘Baptize me in water,’ but I will baptize you in the Spirit.’ He said to him, ‘I see the Spirit descending and remaining on him. This one is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’
I have declared and testified that this is the Son of God.
The next day, John again stood with two of his disciples.
And John said, “Behold, the Lamb of God,”
And when they heard him, these two disciples followed Jesus.
Jesus, and those following Him, turned and said to them, 'What are you seeking?' They said to Him, 'Rabbi, it is said of you, 'You are the one who is to interpret.' Where do you dwell?'
He said to them, 'Come and see.' They came and saw where he was staying, and remained with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
And another of the brothers, Simon, who was called Peter, was among the two who heard from John and followed him.
He found him first of his own brother, Simon, and said to him, 'We have found the Messiah, who is proclaimed as the Christ.'
And he brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, 'You are Simon, son of John. You will be called Peter, which is translated, Stone.'
The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee and found Philip and said to him, 'Follow me.'
And Philip was from Bethsaida, a city of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, 'This is the one about whom Moses wrote in the law, and whom the prophets also spoke: the Son of Joseph from Nazareth.'
And he said to him, ‘Nathanael of Nazareth, can anything good come out of Nazareth?’ Philip said to him, ‘Come and see.’
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said about him, ‘Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit.’
He said to him, 'Philip, how do you know me?' Jesus answered and said to him, 'Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.'
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, 'Rabbi, here is the one about whom Moses and the prophets wrote. This is the Lord, the King of Israel.'
Jesus answered and said to her, “What I told you, keep; believe in me more than these things.”
And He says to him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, from now on you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
